text:
## Abstract
GSE309890 is a gene expression profiling dataset focused on the effects of the antidepressant sertraline on antibiotic resistance in Escherichia coli strain K-12 substr. MG1655. The study investigates how sertraline induces mutations linked to rifampicin and ciprofloxacin resistance, emphasizing metabolic shifts in the pentose phosphate pathway that alter oxidative stress responses and antibiotic susceptibility. The data were obtained from the NCBI GEO database, containing 6 samples of RNA-seq expression data. The main downloadable files include a compressed CSV file of normalized expression values (FPKMs) for all samples. This dataset provides insights into metabolic rewiring in bacteria under drug pressure which has implications for understanding and potentially mitigating antibiotic resistance in clinical and environmental contexts.

## I. Introduction
**Background.** GSE309890 is a gene expression dataset studying the metabolic and genetic mechanisms underlying antibiotic resistance shaped by sertraline, a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor, in E. coli. Antibiotic resistance emergence is a major global health problem, and understanding how non-antibiotic drugs influence this process is crucial.

**Literature Review.** No linked PubMed articles are registered for this dataset, indicating it may be a recent or unpublished study.

**Knowledge Gap.** The metabolic basis by which sertraline accelerates antibiotic resistance and modulates susceptibility had been unclear, particularly concerning the role of the pentose phosphate pathway and oxidative stress.

**Objective & Hypothesis.** The dataset investigates how sertraline biases resistance emergence via metabolic rewiring, hypothesizing that disrupting key enzymes in the pentose phosphate pathway restores antibiotic susceptibility.

## II. Materials and Methods
**Study Design.** Metadata was retrieved from the NCBI GEO database using its accession number GSE309890. Supplementary files and sample details were obtained from the GEO FTP site.

**Materials.** The GEO database was queried via the GEO API tool, downloading metadata and supplementary files list.

**Procedures.** The query "GSE309890" was used to fetch study details, sample counts, FTP directory URLs, and supplementary file information.

**Statistical Analysis.** Not applicable for metadata query.

## III. Results

|-------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Title                   | Antidepressant sertraline biases resistance emergence via stress-driven rewiring of the pentose phosphate pathway       |
| Organism                | Escherichia coli str. K-12 substr. MG1655                                                                               |
| Experiment Type         | Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing                                                                      |
| Publication Date        | 2026-02-01                                                                                                              |
| Number of Samples       | 6                                                                                                                       |
| Samples                 | Replicates from adaptive evolution or control E. coli cultures                                                          |
| Supplementary Files     | GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz (510 KB)                                                                              |
| FTP directory URL       | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/                                                            |
| Supplementary file URL  | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/suppl/GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz                       |
| PubMed linked           | No                                                                                                                      |

The supplementary file is a compressed CSV containing FPKM expression values for all samples.

## IV. Discussion
**Interpretation.** The dataset is a transcriptomic profiling of E. coli exposed to sertraline to understand antibiotic resistance mechanisms. The available data files provide normalized expression quantifications to enable further analysis.

**Context.** This unpublished dataset fills a knowledge gap on how a common antidepressant affects bacterial resistance evolving through metabolic shifts.

**Limitations.** The study metadata lacks a peer-reviewed publication and detailed analysis files beyond expression count matrices. No raw data or detailed sample metadata is included here.

**Conclusion & Future Directions.** GSE309890 provides valuable data for studying sertraline-induced antibiotic resistance. A next step could be integrative analysis with genetic mutation data or testing metabolic inhibition in vitro.

[3] GEO supplementary file: https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/suppl/GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz
